stem:
Nitrogen monoxide, $\text{NO}(\text{g})$, reacts with hydrogen, $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$, under certain conditions.

$$2\text{NO}(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify a change in the reaction mixture that would enable the rate of this reaction to be studied.

The rate equation for this reaction is given.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{NO}]^2[\text{H}_2]$$

The result of an experiment in which NO reacted with $\text{H}_2$ is shown in the table.

| initial $[\text{NO}]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial $[\text{H}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate of reaction/$\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $2.50 \times 10^{-3}$ | $2.50 \times 10^{-3}$ | $1.27 \times 10^{-3}$ |

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Use the data and the rate equation to calculate a value for the rate constant $k$.

Give the units of $k$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
A second experiment is performed at the same temperature. The initial concentration of $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$ is $4.60 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$. The initial rate of the reaction is $2.31 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

Calculate the initial concentration of $\text{NO}(\text{g})$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
State the order of the reaction with respect to $\text{NO}(\text{g})$ and with respect to $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$, and the overall order of the reaction.

| $[\text{NO}]$ |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{H}_2]$ |  |
| overall order |  |

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem:
The reaction is believed to proceed in three steps.

1 $2\text{NO} \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O}_2$

2 $\text{N}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

3 $\text{N}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.text: Deduce which of the three steps is the rate-determining step.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: A third experiment is performed under different conditions. A small amount of $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$ of concentration $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ is mixed with a large excess of $\text{NO}(\text{g})$. The concentration of $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$ is found to have a constant half-life of $2.00$ seconds under the conditions used.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the axes below to construct a graph of the variation in the concentration of $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$ during the first 6 seconds under the conditions used.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: $\text{NO}(\text{g})$ acts as a catalyst in the oxidation of atmospheric sulfur dioxide.

parts.label: (h)(i)
parts.text: Give two equations to describe how $\text{NO}(\text{g})$ acts as a catalyst in this process.

parts.label: (h)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{NO}(\text{g})$ can be described as a catalyst in this reaction.

parts.label: (h)(iii)
parts.text: Describe, with the aid of an equation, an environmental consequence of the oxidation of atmospheric sulfur dioxide.
